reasons: Cited clauses support the compliant classification: Section 10.5 elects the internal laws of the State of New York (and even bars amendment to another governing law), and Section 10.6 submits the parties to the SDNY and New York State courts sitting in New York, New York with venue and forum non conveniens waivers — the preferred position on both law and forum.

No mandatory or foreign-seated arbitration: Article XI mediation/arbitration is elective for the Requesting Party (Section 11.2(a) preserves the right to institute a legal proceeding) and any such proceeding is seated in New York, New York (Section 11.2(d)(i)), so there is no walk-away exposure.
The redline leaves p0426, p0427, p0450 and p0473 textually unchanged and no counterparty comment is proposed, which is what a compliant finding requires.

The rationale correctly treats the 'nonexclusive' submission as a minor sub-element short of the preferred exclusive-jurisdiction wording (and one that preserves our own flexibility) rather than a material deviation; the deterministic governing-law check also confirms the jurisdiction is within the accepted set.
